lessons.title: From sites to symmetry-adapted linear combinations
lessons.summary: Construct the permutation representation yourself, then inspect cancellations, projection, normalization, and construction of the E partners.

sections.title: Step 1: fix the orbital order and operation conventions
sections.text: Four orthonormal scalar orbitals lie at +x, +y, −x and −y. An active C₄z sends site 1 to site 2, so column 1 of the permutation matrix has a 1 in row 2. Generate all eight operations from C₄z and the xz mirror, then verify pairwise that matrix multiplication agrees with the spatial operations.

sections.title: Step 2: use characters to select the required subspaces
sections.text: The trace of each permutation matrix equals the number of orbitals fixed by that operation. Inner products with irreducible characters split the four-dimensional representation into A₁, B₁, and E; the  multiplicity  of A₂ and B₂ are zero. In the character-projection replay, inspect weighted accumulation first and normalize only at the end.
sections.formula: m_α = (1/8) Σ_g χ_α(g)^* χ_D(g)；Γ_D = A₁ ⊕ B₁ ⊕ E

sections.title: Step 3: what do character and partner projections each do?
sections.text: A₁ gives (1,1,1,1)/2 and B₁ gives (1,−1,1,−1)/2. The character projector for E selects only a two-dimensional space. Use P_xx to select E_x, then P_yx to generate E_y, obtaining (1,0,−1,0)/√2 and (0,1,0,−1)/√2. Changing the seed from +x to +y changes the partners obtained, but not the target subspace.
sections.formula: P_α = (d_α/8) Σ_g χ_α(g)^* D(g)；P_mn = (2/8) Σ_g D^(E)_mn(g)^* D(g)

sections.title: Step 4: verify the entire basis rather than memorize symbols
sections.text: Place all SALCs in the columns of U and check U†U=I, projector idempotence and completeness, and simultaneous block decomposition of U†D(g)U. An overall sign or complex phase does not change the subspace, so assignments are graded by column space. With two copies, submit the entire target isotypic subspace rather than just the first copy.

lessons.title: One rule connects polarization, operators, and transitions
lessons.summary: Determine representation containment first, then calculate actual matrix elements. Distinguish forbidden, allowed, and nonzero transitions explicitly.

sections.title: Step 1: specify how the operator transforms
sections.text: In this model, X and Y form the polar-vector representation E; the identity belongs to A₁, X²−Y² to B₁, and the Hermitian circulation operator i(D(C₄)−D(C₄)†)/2 to A₂. Check operator transformations using the actual matrices D(g)O_jD(g)†; an operator's name alone does not determine its behavior in every material.
sections.formula: D(g) O_j D(g)† = Σ_i O_i D^(O)_ij(g)

sections.title: Step 2: calculate the blocks forbidden by group theory
sections.text: The final state representation must be included in tensor product of the operator representation and initial state representation. When the character inner product is 0, the entire coupling block between all partners is zero; greater than 0 simply means that there are forms of coupling allowed by group theory. The table here directly compares each reference SALC block containing multiplicity with the actual square sum.

sections.title: Step 3: Use polarization to calculate the intensity of the allowed block
sections.text: adopts O_θ=cosθ X+sinθ Y. The intensity of copy 1 from A₁ to E_x is cos²θ/2, and to E_y is sin²θ/2, totaling 1/2. The E_y matrix element is zero under x polarization, but the entire A₁→E channel is still allowed; setting the operator amplitude to 0 makes all intensities zero. The angular scan in the figure always corresponds to the dipole probe.

sections.title: Step 4: connect to Wigner–Eckart while distinguishing the groups
sections.text: Finite groups and SU(2) both separate symmetry-fixed geometric structure from system-dependent reduced matrix elements. SU(2) angular-momentum triangle conditions and m selection rules belong to its own representations; SU(2) CG coefficients cannot simply be assigned to C₄ᵥ. Multiple coupling channels or repeated copies require extra channel labels and multiple reduced quantities.

lessons.title: Repeated representations, subgroups, and minimal symmetry breaking
lessons.summary: distinguishes partners and copies in eight-dimensional space, and then uses the real group average to verify when the ban on the parent group is lifted.

sections.title: Step 1: Adding equivalent copies will not add new representation types
sections.text: Two four-orbital sets are each permuted by the same operations, giving 2A₁⊕2B₁⊕2E. Two E partners belong to one two-dimensional irrep, while two E copies belong to multiplicity space. Character projection gives the rank-four E isotypic subspace; projection of one seed gives only one vector.

sections.title: Step 2: Symmetric Hamiltonian can mix copies
sections.text: Hopping between corresponding sites in different copies and an energy offset of the second copy both preserve the parent group. In the E block, the copy-mixing matrix forms a tensor product with the identity in partner space. Mixing thus changes the two energies while preserving each E doublet. Internal rotations of energy eigenvectors do not indicate failed symmetry.

sections.title: Step 3: Regenerate subgroup from reserved generator
sections.text: Retaining C₄z and the mirror gives C₄ᵥ; rotation alone gives C₄, the xz mirror alone gives Cₛ, and removing both gives C₁. Average the B₁-type potential over the retained group before adding it to the Hamiltonian. The result commutes with that subgroup; special parameters may retain additional symmetry. The graph shows these four specified subgroups only.

sections.title: Step 4: diagnose symmetry breaking using matrices rather than deleting labels
sections.text: The minimal-breaking challenge asks when A₁–B₁ mixing ceases to be forbidden by the retained group. Enumerate removed-generator sets, construct the actual subgroup, average the potential and test 〈A₁|V_H|B₁〉. Parent SALCs remain a reference basis after symmetry reduction, but actual energy eigenstates can mix those labels; reassess transitions using operator matrices.

exercises.title: personally constructs the E subspace of four sites
exercises.prompt: Write the matrix action first, then check it with representation-construction replay and subspace assignments.

steps.prompt: Where does C₄z send the +x orbital?
steps.explanation: In the specified site order, D(C₄) has entry 1 in row 2, column 1.

steps.prompt: What irreducible components does this four-dimensional permutation representation contain?
steps.hint: checks the inner product of characters, and the dimensions must also add up to 4.
steps.explanation: Projector ranks are 1,0,1,0,2, giving one copy each of A₁,B₁,E.

steps.prompt: P_E After acting on the +x seed, which is the normalized vector?
steps.hint: E_x has opposite signs on +x and −x.
steps.explanation: character projection first obtains (1,0,−1,0)/2, and after normalization, the denominator becomes √2.

steps.prompt: Should [E_x+E_y,E_x−E_y] pass as a basis for the E subspace?
steps.hint: job compares full column rank space and does not require the same basis vectors.
choices: should pass, the two columns form the same two-dimensional subspace
does not pass, must be equal element by element
does not pass because the two columns are not the original partners.
steps.explanation: reversible internal change of basis maintains projection operator and invariant subspace , normalization can also be reprocessed by the discriminator.

exercises.title: From representation to polarization dependent actual intensity
exercises.prompt: uses a four-site model, unit dipole amplitude and x-polarization, then changes the angle to 45 degrees.

steps.prompt: What representation does the in-plane X and Y operators have in C₄ᵥ?
steps.hint: They combine with each other under rotation.
steps.explanation: two components are transformed according to the Cartesian two-dimensional polar vector matrix.

steps.prompt: Is the A₁→E dipole channel forbidden by group theory?
choices: is only allowed with the B₁ operator
steps.explanation: The final state E appears once in tensor product , but whether it is non-zero still needs to be calculated as a matrix element.

steps.prompt: What are the intensities of the two E partners in x polarization?
steps.hint: X is non-zero only at the ±x site, and E_y is non-zero only at the ±y site.

steps.prompt: After rotating the polarization to 45 degrees, what is the sum of the two intensities?
steps.explanation: Each of the two partners is 1/4, and the total strength remains 1/2. This conclusion is normalized to the full E-partner space and the current model.

exercises.title: What else is protected after the copies are mixed?
exercises.prompt: Compare replica coupling, partner degeneracy, and subgroup constraints using an eight-dimensional preset.

steps.prompt: What are the dimensions of the complete E isotypic subspace in the eight-dimensional model?
steps.hint: Two copies, each E has two partners.
steps.explanation: multiplicity 2 multiplied by the irreducible dimension 2, the projection rank 4 is obtained.

steps.prompt: Can a Hamiltonian keeping C₄ᵥ mix two parts of E?
steps.hint: Schur constraints act on the partner space and do not force the multiplicity space to be diagonal.
choices: Replicas can be mixed but buddy blocks remain the same
No, all copies must be independent
can split two partners of the same E at will
steps.explanation: H_E=H_copy⊗I₂ permits nonzero mixing between copies. Every eigenvalue of the copy-mixing block retains its partner degeneracy.

steps.prompt: Only remove the xz mirror constraint and retain C₄z. Which group is guaranteed to be retained?
steps.hint: takes the closure of the remaining generator .
steps.explanation: C₄z still produces E, C₄z, C₂z and C₄z⁻¹, and they cannot be deleted along with the mirror.

steps.prompt: If a lower-symmetry eigenstate mixes A₁ and B₁, can the A₁ label alone determine all its transitions?
steps.hint: label refers to the parent group reference base, and the actual state has been mixed.
choices: No, you must use reserved groups or actual state matrix elements.
Yes, only the label with the largest component is retained
Yes, parent group tags can never be mixed.
steps.explanation: It is necessary to recheck the subgroup representation and the operators in the actual energy eigenbase; the parent group SALC is still a legal calculation basis.

cases.title: Square coordination local environment: four ligand combination
cases.summary: combines four scalar orbitals of equivalent ligand orientations into A₁, B₁ and E, with polarization connected to the local crystal field and orbital courses.
cases.assumption: only uses the C₄ᵥ subgroup with four scalar orbitals. True square plane coordination is possible with higher symmetries; in this example there is no central atomic orbital, chemical overlap, inverted parity, or material fit.

cases.title: Two sets of local orbits: partners and copies are not the same thing
cases.summary: Mix two equivalent orbital sets through hopping between corresponding sites; inspect E-partner degeneracy and copy-energy splitting, then submit the full four-dimensional E subspace.
cases.assumption: can represent two sets of base orbitals with the same transformation properties; the upper and lower layers in the figure are only used to distinguish the copies and do not mean that the real double-layer crystal space group has been determined.

cases.title: Local anisotropy: lifting the ban on parent group mixing
cases.summary: Use a B₁-type onsite potential to connect SALC construction, orbital splitting, order parameters and optical selection rules. Predict the fewest generator removals, then inspect actual matrix blocks.
cases.assumption: perturbation is a given X²−Y² type potential; the distortion amplitude is not derived from elastic constants or first principles, nor is the complete space group subgroup relationship automatically established.
